I recommend that anyone not considering a purchase, especially those easily swayed, avoid this place. Based on reviews, the persistence, aggressive sales tactics regarding loans, and selective customer selection are all accurate.

I already have a dog, and while I wasn't looking to get another one immediately, I wanted to consider adopting one, which is why I visited this shop. It was a mistake to go in; I was relentlessly pressured, and although I wanted to see other dogs, they immediately picked out the one I initially said was cute and let me hold it.

I've been to many pet shops, but the sales pressure here was absolutely terrible.

The salesperson was a slightly overweight woman with dyed hair.

I personally prefer to pay in full if possible.

The woman said that even if I was worried about the credit check, other people had been able to get loans through several different companies.

The dogs were certainly cute, and I even considered taking out a loan.

However, personally, I couldn't understand why someone without money or resources would rush into taking out a loan to get a pet. While listening to their aggressive sales pitch, I felt I didn't want to buy from them.

After listening for several tens of minutes, I tried to leave, but they semi-forced me to pay a deposit for a family meeting. I was still considering it at the time, so I left the store.

I hadn't decided to buy at all, and I had said I wanted to wait until I moved within Tokyo before getting a pet, yet they said things like, "If you decide to buy, you can take it home right away," which made me suspicious.

I'm not familiar with the detailed rules of pet shops, but with the pet I previously adopted, it took about two days after deciding to purchase to ensure there were no health problems.

Even though nothing was ready, they said, "You can take this pet home when you go back to your parents' house!" I felt their treatment of animals was terrible. They said they owned pets themselves, but they didn't seem to have much compassion for animals. I suppose they say things like that to push a sale because it's their job.

Later, after thinking it over, I went back to the store to cancel and explain the situation.

The reason is that my family already has two dogs, one of which is a puppy, so it would be difficult to dedicate enough time and training to a new dog.

Then they said, "The only thing that will change if you get a new dog is the number of food bowls."

Are they making fun of animals?

There are other things that take time, such as vaccinations, vet visits, and training, so I was completely put off.

First of all, despite explaining that my family and I can't dedicate enough time due to work, they spoke very desperately about how they needed to sell the dog, which made me feel very uncomfortable.

And the way they completely changed their attitude after returning the deposit was incredible (lol). I've never experienced such customer service in any store I've been to before. Of course, this includes stores other than pet shops as well.

My companion and I were both completely put off.

I thought they were a fairly good store, but I think Pets First and Coolik have much better customer service. There are many cute puppies there, but I don't want to buy from someone like this, so I will never visit again, and I'm glad I didn't take one home right away, so I'm posting this as a warning.
